episodes.180303: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a weak boundary. A few areas received multiple rounds of storms, resulting in isolated instances of flash flooding and flooding.
episodes.180327: Extreme instability developed during the day which lead to widespread thunderstorm development in an environment with little to no winds aloft.
episodes.180334: An upper level trough tracked across the Northern Rockies, dragging its base across the Western Slope. This resulted in increased instability which fueled scattered showers and thunderstorms. Convection was high-based given the abundance of dry air at the lower levels. Strong outflow from collapsing storms produced gusty winds which resulted in some damage across portions of Moffat County.
episodes.180369: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced wind damage near Rembert, SC.
episodes.180444: Thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain in southwestern New Jersey during the late afternoon and early evening of July 4.  Rainfall totals were as high as 2.0 to 3.5 inches.
episodes.180719: Following scattered convection throughout the afternoon hours, a more cohesive squall line formed over Utah's West Desert region. This squall progressed eastward through the northern portions of the state, resulting in a swath of strong to very strong wind gusts, due in part to low dew points and dry low levels of the atmosphere.
episodes.180806: Thunderstorms with strong outflow winds developed across Carbon County during the afternoon of the 3rd continuing northeast into east-central Wyoming through the evening.
episodes.180809: Thunderstorms with strong outflow winds moved across the northern Nebraska Panhandle as a squall line developed farther west in east-central Wyoming early in the evening on the 3rd.
episodes.181207: A weak disturbance passed through West Virginia on July 4th, resulting in showers and isolated thunderstorms. Moderate to heavy rainfall, combined with back building of storms, caused flash flooding in Calhoun and Roane Counties during the evening. Once storms departed eastward, high water issues dwindled.
episodes.181269: A severe thunderstorm tracked across portions of southern Campbell County, producing hail to golf ball size in the Wright area.
episodes.181270: A severe thunderstorm developed over north central Campbell County and tracked east-southeast through southern Crook County. The storm produced hail to ping pong ball size.
episodes.181272: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed over far southeastern Campbell and southern Weston Counties, bringing strong wind gusts and hail to quarter size.
episodes.181274: A thunderstorm became severe as it tracked into southwestern Crook County. The storm produced wind gusts to 60 mph near Pine Haven.
episodes.181279: A severe thunderstorm quickly developed over the northern Black Hills and moved south-southeast into portions of the central Black Hills. The storm produced large hail to golf ball size.
episodes.181281: A severe thunderstorm developed quickly across far southern portions of Rapid City and tracked south-southeast across the eastern foothills and adjacent plains. The storm produced hail as large as baseballs east of Rockerville. As the storm weakened, wind gusts to 60 mph developed over the plains.
episodes.181283: A line of severe thunderstorms developed across Wyoming and tracked east-northeast across southwestern and west central South Dakota during the mid to late evening hours. The storms primarily produced wind gusts around 70 mph, with some small hail as well.
episodes.181583: A surface trough and embedded surface wave led to the development of isolated to scattered thunderstorms over the eastern Sandhills and southern Coastal Plain in the mid to late-evening hours. Some trees were reported down due to strong winds over Sampson and Cumberland counties.
episodes.181598: A slow moving front and a very moist airmass yielded slow moving thunderstorms that dumped heavy rain over southeast Wyoming county with portions of park roads and hiking trails flooded at Letchworth State Park. The front then stalled out during the evening along the New York and Pennsylvania state line leading to multiple rounds of slow moving thunderstorms crossing the same areas with drenching rains. Significant flash flooding occurred over southwest Allegany county in Bolivar and Richburg, where some roads were washed out. Some of these road closures may last for a while.
episodes.181644: A social media report and attached photos documented damaging winds from a severe thunderstorms that moved through South Range during the early evening of the 4th.
episodes.181698: SW steering flow pushed the dominant west coast sea breeze inland with a merger between the Highway 301 and St. Johns River basin during the evening. A moist and unstable airmass near the collision produced a few strong to pulse severe storms.
episodes.181737: Following scattered convection throughout the afternoon hours, a more cohesive squall line formed over Utah's West Desert region. This squall progressed eastward through the northern portions of Utah during the evening, and subsequently pushed into southwest Wyoming thereafter. This squall resulted in a swath of strong to very strong wind gusts, due in part to low dew points and dry low levels of the atmosphere. The same pattern responsible for the strong widespread squall event also yielded isolated strong wind gusts the morning of July 4 with additional decaying convection.
episodes.181757: Flows along the middle James River continued to be elevated, although mostly below flood stage, for the month of July. The James River at Huron briefly rose above flood stage early in the month.
episodes.181865: A cold front sparked a few lines of thunderstorms. These thunderstorms produced localized wind damage, most notably over northeastern Maryland during the early evening hours.
episodes.181866: A cold front sparked a few lines of thunderstorms. These thunderstorms produced localized wind damage, most notably over northeastern Maryland during the early evening hours.
episodes.181923: Widespread severe weather was observed across Eastern Nebraska on the afternoon and evening of July 4. Storms initially were discrete or multi-clustered and produced mainly hail. The largest hail report was 2.75 inches near Tarnov in Platte County. A QLCS formed as storms merged along a cold front and strong wind gusts became the primary hazard. Numerous locations observed 60+ mph wind gusts. An estimated peak wind gust of 80 mph caused damage to trees and power poles near Weston.
episodes.181936: A cold front sparked a few lines of thunderstorms. These thunderstorms produced localized gale- to storm-force winds.
episodes.181961: An isolated intense supercell thunderstorm tracked across Goshen County during the early to mid afternoon on 7/4, producing a swath of large hail as well as destructive straight line winds which produced damage consistent with 90+ MPH gusts near the town of Veteran. Later, a second line of thunderstorms swept across Carbon, Albany, and eventually western Laramie counties during the late afternoon and early evening, producing a broad area of 45+ MPH wind gusts with embedded pockets of gusts exceeding 60 MPH.
episodes.181964: An isolated severe storm tracked across portions of Scotts Bluff and Banner counties during the mid-afternoon on 7/4.
episodes.182027: Evening seabreeze thunderstorm produced a strong marine wind gust in Lee County.
episodes.182082: The combination of an upper-level disturbance and nearby surface low and frontal boundary resulted in isolated showers and thunderstorms across portions of eastern New York on July 4, 2023. A few of these thunderstorms became severe producing downed trees and wires. A more concentrated area of damage occurred from the Rensselaer/Columbia County line southward to Styvesant. A NWS Storm Survey confirmed a straight line wind event occurred with winds estimated up to 100 mph causing widespread damage.
episodes.182107: A cold front moved eastward from the Ohio Valley during the afternoon of July 3, 2023, which led to an organized line of thunderstorms advancing into the region. Abundant moisture an very warm temperatures created an environment that supported strong downdraft winds from thunderstorms. As the increased moisture converged along the higher terrain of the mountains, scattered thunderstorms developed, and caused pockets of wind damage.
episodes.182109: An upper level trough was over the northern Rocky Mountains and Northern Plains and was bringing a cold front south through Nebraska during the afternoon and evening hours of Independence Day. Temperatures heated up in advance of the front with dewpoints mostly in the 60s. A very moist and unstable atmosphere was present. CAPE values were generally near 4,000 J/kg ahead of the front, and 0 to 6 km wind shear values were around 35 knots. Mid-level lapse rates were generally 7 to 8 degrees C/km. ||Isolated showers and storms were moving across portions of south central Nebraska during the early to mid-afternoon hours. This activity did not produce any severe weather. The main storm activity developed late in the afternoon into the evening hours and was associated with the cold front moving through Nebraska. Storms began developing in central Nebraska in the late afternoon and early evening hours. Then storms developed in south central Nebraska and formed a line with the storms in the central part of the state. The storms in central Nebraska moved southeast during the evening hours while the storms in the south central part of the state remained fairly stationary. The storms produced large hail and wind gusts of 58 to 66 mph between 5:30 PM CDT and 9 PM CDT. The largest hail reported was up to 2.50 inches and was reported in Webster, Fillmore, and Thayer Counties.
episodes.182110: An upper level trough was over the northern Rocky Mountains and Northern Plains and was bringing a cold front south into Kansas during the early evening hours of Independence Day. Temperatures heated up in advance of the front with dewpoints mostly in the 60s. A very moist and unstable atmosphere was present. CAPE values were generally near 4,000 J/kg ahead of the front, and 0 to 6 km wind shear values were around 35 knots. Mid-level lapse rates were generally 7 to 8 degrees C/km.||A storm developed and produced golf ball sized hail in Smith County in north central Kansas at 4:45 PM CDT. This was the biggest hail of the day in north central Kansas. This storm continued to grow in size and then split apart with one part of the storm moving to the west and the other part moving to the east. The east moving storm began moving southeast and formed into a bowing structure. This storm produced winds ranging from 58 mph to 71 mph in Phillips and Osborne Counties. The severe reports ended with a 68 mph wind gust in Phillips County just before 8 PM CDT.
episodes.182127: Despite weak surface forcing, hot and humid conditions led to scattered, slow-moving thunderstorms developing by mid-afternoon on July 4th. While most of these storms were below severe limits, one instance of wind damage occurred in McLean County.
episodes.182249: On July 4, showers and thunderstorms developed across most of the state around noon.  The line of storms across southern New Hampshire contained localized downpours that dropped 2 to 3��� over a 3 hour period in Stoddard and Wolfeboro.  Additional flooding was reported in both of these towns during the early afternoon hours with road flooding and erosion damage being reported.  Across northern New Hampshire isolated thunderstorm downpours were estimated to drop up to 2��� in an hour in the rural mountains of Coos County and near Mount Moosilauke in the White Mountains National Forest.  Heavy rain showers and thunderstorms were isolated into the evening hours in the Connecticut River Valley but no additional flooding was reported in these areas.  In addition, a few isolated storms around the state become severe with sporadic tree damage due to wind damage, along with a few reports of low end severe hail.
episodes.182616: An area of low pressure over northern Manitoba trailed a cold front across the Northland on July 3rd. Storms developed ahead of the front during the afternoon and evening hours with storms becoming strong to severe across northwest Wisconsin. These storms took on a linear mode with an associated damaging wind threat as they moved across the region. These damaging winds led to reports of downed trees and powerlines as they progressed to the east.
episodes.182677: A cold front approached the region, with scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developing out ahead of it, producing damaging wind gusts across parts of New Jersey.
episodes.182678: A cold front approached the region, with scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developing out ahead of it, producing damaging wind gusts across parts of Delaware.
episodes.182680: A weak system moved through the area on the 4th of July, sparking off scattered showers and thunderstorms. A few storms reached severe levels in New Jersey, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.182896: A trough across the southern Rocky Mountains helped develop afternoon strong to severe thunderstorms across the higher elevations and adjacent plains. Isolated severe wind gusts were reported.
episodes.182916: An area of low pressure over central South Dakota, with a stationary front eastward along Interstate 90, brought periods of thunderstorms late on July 3rd through the early morning hours on July 4th. The storms produced isolated severe weather with golf ball size hail near Florence and a 77 mph wind gust near Gann Valley.
episodes.182975: A mid level trough and a quasi-stationary boundary across Southern New England led to widespread flash flooding in the late hours of the 3rd into the 4th. Most of the flooding was in Rhode Island and Connecticut where cars became stuck in water, and several basements were flooded. In MA a few roads were closed.
episodes.182976: A mid level trough and a quasi-stationary boundary across Southern New England led to widespread flash flooding in the late hours of the 3rd into the 4th. Most of the flooding was in Rhode Island and Connecticut where cars became stuck in water, and several basements were flooded. In MA a few roads were closed.
episodes.182977: A mid level trough and a quasi-stationary boundary across Southern New England led to widespread flash flooding in the late hours of the 3rd into the 4th. Most of the flooding was in Rhode Island and Connecticut where cars became stuck in water, and several basements were flooded. In MA a few roads were closed.
episodes.182982: A few thunderstorms developed during the afternoon, with one particular storm becoming severe and producing damaging winds.
episodes.182996: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.183252: Mother Nature supplied most of the fireworks for the Fourth of July as severe thunderstorms moved across the region during the late afternoon and evening.  Intense wind gusts, locally heavy rain and minor street flooding accompanied the storms.  Denver Fire performed a swift water rescue in the area of 38th Avenue and Fox Street, in the evening when a motorist became stranded in their vehicle.  Several fireworks shows were either cancelled or postponed due to safety concerns associated with the inclement weather.  Peak wind gusts included:  74 mph northwest of Red Feather Lakes, 70 mph just northeast of Kremmling, and 67 mph at Buckley AFB.  Several areas along the urban corridor picked up anywhere from 1 to 2 inches of rainfall.  At Denver International Airport, a storm produced 0.77 inch of rainfall along with a peak wind gust to 54 mph.
episodes.183254: Parts of Sheridan and Cherry Counties got brushed by a linear system moving from the panhandle into South Dakota during the late evening hours of July 3, resulting in isolated severe wind gusts.
episodes.183277: A weak upper level trough remained stagnant over North and Central Texas during the first week of July, generating isolated thunderstorms each afternoon. A few storms produced marginally severe hail and wind damage on the 3rd and 4th of July, while one slow-moving storm cluster produced flash flooding in Denton County.
episodes.183296: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along and south of I-40 due to diurnal heating during the late afternoon on July 4, 2023. Weak wind shear combined with deep moisture produced slow-moving, highly efficient rainfall-producing thunderstorms. There were several reports of flash flooding across the area.
episodes.183449: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of central, eastern and southeast Virginia.
episodes.183557: A slow moving front and shortwave trough aloft approached from the west. Surface heating led to moderate instability and severe thunderstorms were able to develop and produce damaging wind gusts and large hail as they moved through southern CT.
episodes.183558: A slow moving front and shortwave trough aloft approached from the west. Surface heating led to moderate instability and a severe thunderstorm was able to develop and produce damaging wind gusts as it moved over the waters.
episodes.183586: A stalled frontal boundary over the area provided a focus for convection to develop in the afternoon on July 4th. CAPE values of greater than 2000 J/kg and PWAT values near 1.8-2 allowed thunderstorms that developed along the stationary front to slowly drift southward while producing torrential rainfall rates of 1-2 per hour. Some areas saw 1-3 of rain over a 1 to 3 hour period which produced localized flash flooding.
episodes.183587: A stalled frontal boundary over the area provided a focus for convection to develop in the afternoon on July 4th. CAPE values of greater than 2000 J/kg and PWAT values near 1.8-2 allowed thunderstorms that developed along the stationary front to slowly drift southward while producing torrential rainfall rates of 1-2 per hour. Some areas saw 1-3 of rain over a 1 to 3 hour period which produced localized flash flooding.
episodes.183603: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across eastern Minnesota and western Wisconsin. A few of the stronger storms produced some large hail and wind damage.
episodes.183604: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across eastern Minnesota and western Wisconsin. A few of the stronger storms produced some large hail and wind damage.
episodes.183621: A weakening line of storms moved across the region during the late morning and produced minor wind damage near New Richmond. This was followed by another storm in the afternoon that produced a funnel cloud, with one report of tree damage. A tornado warning was issued, but there were no confirmed tornadoes.
episodes.183626: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.183629: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours along a stationary front across portions of southeast South Carolina. A few of these thunderstorms became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183668: Afternoon and early evening thunderstorms focused along a weak surface boundary from southwest Minnesota into areas south of Interstate 90 in southeast South Dakota.  Even with very weak deep-layer shear, modest surface-based instability of 1500-2000 J/kg led to the rapid development of storms, which peaked in mainly hail producing severity early in the life cycle, as well as an erratic tornado in eastern Bon Homme County.
episodes.183676: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the latter half of the afternoon along a slow moving cold front.  Dry air poised off the surface allowed for outflow dominant storms to develop, with a brief period of damaging gusty wind.
episodes.183677: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the latter half of the afternoon along a slow moving cold front. Dry air poised off the surface allowed for outflow dominant storms to develop, with a brief period of damaging gusty wind.
episodes.183933: A strong cold front and shortwave moved across Wyoming. Showers and thunderstorms mixed strong low level winds to the surface and brought numerous reports of wind gusts over 50 mph. The highest wind occurred in the Wind River Range where favored channeling brought wind gusts as high as 96 mph. In the lower elevations, the highest wind gust was 80 mph to the north of Casper. Wind gusts over 58 mph occurred in Fremont, Teton, Natrona, Sublette and Sweetwater Counties. In Fremont County, the wind capsized a kayak and threw two men into the water at Ocean Lake. One man could not be rescued and was presumed drowned. On the north shore of Lake Yellowstone, a microburst downed hundreds of trees in the Lake Village area of the park, blocking roads and causing a loss of power for multiple days.
episodes.183963: Scattered thunderstorms developed along the Blue Ridge during the afternoon and evening and moved southeast across the Upstate. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in the foothills.
episodes.184008: A stalled frontal boundary over the area provided a focus for convection to develop and move over southeast NY. One storm produced frequent lightning.
episodes.184053: A mid atmospheric disturbance moved over a unstable airmass across northern New York during the afternoon hours of July 4th. Scattered thunderstorms rotated north to southeast across the region, some of them providing localized damaging winds.
episodes.184056: A mid atmospheric disturbance moved over a unstable airmass across northern Vermont during the afternoon hours of July 4th. Scattered thunderstorms rotated north to southeast across the region, some of them providing localized damaging winds.
episodes.184087: A thunderstorm produced heavy rain near central Morristown. Clogged culverts limited drainage.
episodes.184094: A weak trough of 500 MB low pressure helped trigger locally heavy rains over western portions of the Tennessee Valley.
episodes.184126: Residual moisture from an incredibly anomalously wet June continues to moisten the lower levels aiding in ample amounts of instability. The northwest flow pattern created a lot of shear, which led to prolonged 3 day severe weather event over adjacent and eastern plains of southern Colorado.
episodes.184268: Scattered storms developed each afternoon hours and a few became strong to severe which downed some trees.
episodes.184335: A large complex of thunderstorms moved across northern Kansas into central Kansas and southeast Kansas during the evening hours of July 4th, 2023.  The line of thunderstorms produced damaging wind reports and a few large hail reports. The complex of storms also brought heavy rainfall to some areas.
episodes.184380: Severe storms slowly sagged southeast through the Mississippi River Valley during the late night hours of July 3rd. The storms gradually weakened as they progressed through western Wisconsin, with a single report of multiple fallen trees at Lake Neshonoc (La Crosse County).
episodes.184590: A southwest to northeast corridor of storm activity occurred during the afternoon through early evening across Northwest Kansas.  The largest hail reported from these storms was near Tasco.  The dry, loose ground, combined with the thunderstorms winds produced near zero visibility near Monument and Selkirk.  Wind gusts up to an estimated 90 MPH near Norton blew the roof off of a cabin.  Lastly, a landspout occurred along the west edge of the thunderstorm activity north of Tribune.
episodes.184862: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms impacted the inland sounds and rivers as well as the coastal waters north of Core Banks during the afternoon and early evening on July 4th.
